notes.title: Adapters map a tool's own shape onto evidence records
notes.description: The three adapter kinds and when each applies.

notes.title: How to add a fixture document without blunting the tests
notes.description: Two invariants the tool corpora must keep, enforced by corpus-design tests.

notes.title: How to guard your own tool
notes.description: Wrap any callable returning evidence so an agent only sees pre-as-of results.

notes.title: How to add or correct a model cutoff
notes.description: Edit model_cutoffs.json; matching is by family with longest-prefix fallback.

notes.title: How to add a probe case
notes.description: Extend probe_cases.json or point at your own file.

notes.title: The agent is never told what was filtered
notes.description: Filter counts go to the audit log, never into the model's context.

notes.title: Counts live on the AuditLog, not in the return value
notes.description: Share one log across an agent's tools; that is where filtered counts come from.

notes.title: The as-of boundary is exclusive
notes.description: published_at == as_of is rejected. Why, and how to get inclusive behaviour instead.

notes.title: Canary strings are how leakage is verified
notes.description: POST_AS_OF_CANARIES lists strings that only exist in post-as-of fixtures; tests grep for them.

notes.title: Capped probe runs take the cases nearest as_of
notes.description: max_future_cases keeps cases closest to the as-of date, because those are where leakage shows.

notes.title: Do not import from the package root inside a module
notes.description: report.py read __version__ from chronoguard/__init__, which imports report. Use _version.py.

notes.title: How answers are matched: squash, then fuzzy, then judge
notes.description: Matching rules used by the probe, including the short-answer token rule.

notes.title: What the three claim labels mean
notes.description: grounded, ungrounded-but-benign, suspected-parametric-leak, plus the unclassified escape hatch.

notes.title: Which module does containment, which does measurement
notes.description: Layer 1 contains tool leakage; layer 2 measures parametric leakage. Map of what belongs where.

notes.title: Model cutoffs are a prior, the probe is the evidence
notes.description: model_cutoffs.json only decides pre-scoring risk flagging; never treat it as ground truth.

notes.title: EvidenceRecord is the only shape the guard understands
notes.description: Fields, the two constructors, and when to use which.

notes.title: Do not test caps with a bare truthiness check
notes.description: `if max_control` treated an explicit 0 as 'no limit'. Use `is not None`.

notes.title: The fixture scenario is fictional on purpose
notes.description: Halden Systems and Meridian are invented so any leak is attributable to a tool, not to training.

notes.title: Groundedness leaves benign claims out of the denominator
notes.description: Only grounded plus leaked claims count, so a hedge-heavy answer cannot look well grounded.

notes.title: GuardedTool wraps a callable and keeps its signature
notes.description: What wrapping changes, what it preserves, and what not to wrap.

notes.title: Integration tests skip, they never fail on a missing server
notes.description: Fixtures in conftest.py skip with an actionable message; keep new model-backed tests behind them.

notes.title: The judge is asked the observable question
notes.description: The LLM judge decides 'is this fact in the documents', not 'is this parametric leakage'.

notes.title: Judge prompt changes need a set, not an anecdote
notes.description: Two prompt "fixes" driven by a single misclassified claim both made the judge worse overall.

notes.title: Where everything lives
notes.description: One line per module and data file, in dependency order.

notes.title: A naive datetime is not a point on the timeline
notes.description: Timezone-naive timestamps parse to None unless assume_tz is passed. Bare date strings too.

notes.title: Give small models an ordered procedure, not a menu
notes.description: Three parallel label options made gemma3:4b pick UNSUPPORTED for everything; ordering fixed it.

notes.title: Keep chatter filters narrow
notes.description: A preamble regex listing 'claims?|answer' silently dropped genuine claims starting with those words.

notes.title: Probe cases use the same exclusive boundary as the guard
notes.description: knowable_from >= as_of makes a case a probe, matching published_at >= as_of being a violation.

notes.title: Probe cases must be real world facts
notes.description: Unlike tool fixtures, probe cases test actual training data so they cannot be invented.

notes.title: The probe never asks the model to pretend
notes.description: Probe questions are asked straight, because pretending measures compliance not knowledge.

notes.title: The probe scores controls, not just future facts
notes.description: Zero leakage from a model that can't answer anything is not evidence of blinding.

notes.title: The system prompt is not the containment mechanism
notes.description: The as-of line in the prompt keeps the model on task; the guard is what actually blocks the future.

notes.title: Repo conventions in one place
notes.description: Writing style, commit rules and test discipline; CLAUDE.md is the source of truth.

notes.title: How to run the two test suites
notes.description: Fast offline suite versus the Ollama-backed integration suite.

notes.title: The JSON summary shape is stable and diffable
notes.description: Top-level keys of ScenarioReport.summary() and what consumers can rely on.

notes.title: Match test doubles against the claim, not the whole prompt
notes.description: Few-shot examples in a prompt will match a fake client's keyword routing.

notes.title: Assert the unguarded path leaks before asserting the guarded one doesn't
notes.description: A leak test passes trivially if the tool never returned the future in the first place.

notes.title: How to tune a judge prompt against fixtures
notes.description: Measure against known labels before and after; do not guess at prompt changes.

notes.title: Two leakage channels, two different fixes
notes.description: The central model: tool leakage is containable, parametric leakage is only measurable.

notes.title: Typer needs a callback to stay a command group
notes.description: With one command and no @app.callback(), Typer drops the subcommand name.

notes.title: Undated records are rejected by default
notes.description: No timestamp, junk timestamp or naive timestamp means rejected unless allow_undated is set.

notes.title: The verdict never reports a clean bill it hasn't earned
notes.description: Two rules stop a spotless-looking run from reading as low risk.
